findings.body: The previous gap remains: baselines and successful submissions retain every seen ID, and session.end never deletes obsolete session keys. The unchanged src/forge/board.py:289–300 exposes historical run endings, so each session copies an increasing history. Claude's [pinned store contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/684800b206824dfd0cc8a876e8604b20f72c3617/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts) rejects writes exceeding 4 MiB across the plugin store. Once that limit is reached, acknowledgement can fail after submission succeeds, causing the same batch to be submitted again; new-session baselines also fail. Bound retained history and obsolete session keys while preserving deduplication.
findings.title: Bound persisted seen history before Claude's store limit

findings.body: The previous routing gap remains. forge.toml:6 and .github/workflows/forge-next.yml:58 run pytest, while tests/test_mod_plugin.py:45–57 only typechecks the native tests. The packaged cases exercise real occurrences, shared-store sessions and reload batching, but submission-failure retries, worker/headless gating and session resets still depend on native assertions that the automated suite does not execute. plans/FORGE-MOD-1.md:284 assigns the plugin CI job to SHIP; that task must execute these tests and propagate failures. This remains P2 advice under the task-ownership ruling.
findings.title: Later: SHIP must run the native event tests in CI
